page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration instructions. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, requiring network-attached persistent storage for stateful workloads.

Synthetic benchmark metrics demonstrate exceptional single-core processing capabilities contrasted against bounded multi-core and memory subsystem throughput. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a top-tier single-core score of 2319.0, excelling particularly in text processing and single-threaded data compression workloads such as gzip at 35.15 GB/sec. However, multi-core throughput reflects the small core count, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5163.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 6532.16. Memory subsystem performance is modest, scoring in lower percentiles on PassMark memory benchmarks, with large-block memory read bandwidth measured at 38.47 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, c4-highcpu-4 optimizes per-core compute power for workloads that rely heavily on single-thread execution rather than expansive parallel scaling or heavy in-memory caching. Web serving reaches 8.75 GB/sec and Redis key-value workloads achieve 6.25 million SET operations per second. The server is well positioned for continuous integration tasks, Clang build environments, lightweight API gateways, and web application frontends where high single-threaded responsiveness is required without the cost of surplus RAM.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. Configured with 8.0 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, but does not provide local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark assessments, the instance displays superior single-core responsiveness, reaching a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2319.0 and strong single-threaded gzip throughput of 35.15 GB/sec. Conversely, memory bandwidth and aggregate multi-core throughput remain bounded by the 4-vCPU footprint, reflected in lower PassMark memory and CPU scores. With web serving throughput of 8.75 GB/sec and Redis performance reaching 6.25 million operations per second, c4-highcpu-4 represents an efficient profile for CPU-bound single-thread tasks, build automation, CI/CD runners, and lightweight web serving.
